thumb_sub: Turn it over. Go and tell
hook: How to help a five year old tell you when a screen upsets them

caps: Hello, I'm DiGi. This one's for you and your grown up.
Snuggle up. Ready?
Before we start, let's do our big breath.
Breathe in, and out.
Lovely. Now, my memory question.
Last time we learned something very important.
When a message pops up on a screen, who is on the other side?
A real person. That's right.
A real person with real feelings.
And guess what? You have real feelings too.
That's what today is all about.
Today we learn one big thing.
Screens can give us big feelings.
And when a screen gives you a yucky feeling,
you'll know just what to do.
Say our special word. Feeling.
Screens can give us lots of feelings.
Sometimes we watch something funny and our tummy feels happy and giggly.
That's a lovely feeling.
But sometimes, not very often, a screen shows something
that makes our tummy feel yucky.
A bit wobbly. A bit sad. Or a bit worried.
Maybe a scary picture pops up.
Maybe someone says something unkind in a game.
Maybe a video just feels wrong.
I call that the uh oh feeling.
And here's a secret. Your body is very clever.
When something isn't right, your body tells you.
Your tummy might feel funny. Your heart might go fast.
You might want to look away.
That's not you being silly.
That's your body being a good helper.
And if your tummy does not say anything, but something still seems wrong,
you can still turn it over and tell.
Pause me here. And grown up, ask your little one:
where do you feel a wobbly feeling?
lines.say: Pause me here. And grown up, ask your little one: Where do you feel a wobbly feeling?

caps: Point to it. Point to where the feeling lives.
I'll wait.
So what do we do when the uh oh feeling comes?
Just two little steps. Ready?
Step one. Turn it over.
Turn the screen over so you can't see it.
Step two. Go and tell your grown up.
That's it.
You don't have to work out why the feeling came.
You don't have to fix it all by yourself.
Turning it over and telling.
That's the whole job, and you can do it.
Here's a lovely thing you might hear tonight.
A child might say,
"Something on the screen made me feel yucky."
And the grown up says, warm as anything,
"Thank you for telling me.
lines.say: And the grown up says, warm as anything, Thank you for telling me.

caps: You are never in trouble for telling me.
I'm so glad you did."
Did you hear that?
Telling is never naughty.
A yucky feeling doesn't mean you did something wrong.
It means your clever body is asking for help.
And when you tell your grown up,
they can help you feel better.
Grown up, this one's yours to say.
Pause me and tell them,
"If a screen ever gives you the uh oh feeling,
you can always come to me.
You will never be in trouble."
Say it slowly, like you mean it.
They'll remember it forever.
Now our special sentence.
Three times, big voices!
Turn it over. Go and tell.
Turn it over. Go and tell.
Turn it over. Go and tell.
Tonight, play the high five game.
Grown up, you call out, "Uh oh feeling!"
Little one, turn a screen face down.
Then run as fast as you can and give your grown up a great big high five.
Do it two or three times, giggling all the way.
Now your body knows exactly what to do without even thinking.
Before I go, show your grown up one thing you remember from today.
Anything at all.
Got it? Brilliant.
And grown up, every time they run to you instead of hiding,
that's your win. Keep the door open.
Remember, little one, all your feelings are okay.
Every single one.
And remember, screens are better together.
See you next time.
